I'm Ishita, and I share a wall with Neelam's flat. In March Neelam's uncle bought her a costly scooter for the new job, and she was delighted, taking the whole floor for a ride. By June he had begun phoning. One evening I heard through the wall: "Uncle, thank you again for the scooter. I will always be grateful. I can drive your daughter to coaching on Saturdays, but not every evening."
Then quiet. I don't know what Neelam felt. But the next week the scooter was in the parking lot as usual, and Neelam still went to the evening class every Tuesday. The uncle's number came up on the screen a few more times, and the tone at the door was polite.

qa.a: He bought the scooter in March.

qa.q: What might Neelam have felt when the uncle's calls began in June?
qa.a: Neelam may have felt pressured or uneasy, though the narrator says they cannot know for sure what Neelam felt.

qa.q: What choice did Neelam make on the phone that kept the relationship clean?
qa.a: Neelam thanked the uncle again, offered to drive his daughter to coaching on Saturdays, and declined every evening, so the gift did not become control.

qa.q: How might Ishita's view of Neelam's call differ from Neelam's own experience?
qa.a: Ishita only heard through the wall and cannot know Neelam's feelings, so Ishita sees the polite refusal but not what it cost Neelam.

grounding: A young adult gets a costly gift from a relative that later becomes a reason for favours, and accepts kindly while keeping freedom.

passage:
Workplace mentor's note, Thursday.
Kunal, 24, asked to speak privately. Last year his uncle Vaibhav bought him a motorbike when he got his first job, "as a blessing." Now the uncle expects Kunal to spend every weekend at his shop, and to leave his job next year to join the family business.
Kunal said, "When I say no, he says, 'After everything I've done for you?' I feel like I've been bought."
He looked miserable. I asked what he wanted. "To keep my job. And to keep my uncle."
We talked through options: thanking his uncle sincerely; offering to help at the shop one Sunday a month, by choice; and, if the pressure continues, offering to pay back the bike's value over time so the gift stops carrying a debt.
Next step: Kunal will talk to his uncle, with his mother present, this weekend.

qa.q: What did Kunal's uncle buy him?
qa.a: His uncle Vaibhav bought him a motorbike, "as a blessing."

qa.q: What was Kunal feeling when he said he felt like he'd been bought?
qa.a: Kunal felt trapped and miserable, pressured by the gift into favours he didn't want to give.

qa.q: What options did Kunal and the mentor discuss, and why might they help?
qa.a: Thanking the uncle, offering limited help by choice, and paying back the bike's value if needed could keep Kunal's freedom while keeping the relationship clean.

qa.q: How might Vaibhav see the situation?
qa.a: Vaibhav probably feels he gave generously and deserves loyalty, so he may be hurt when Kunal says no.

grounding: A mentor's note shows a young adult whose relative's costly gift turns into a reason for control, and ways to keep the relationship clean.

passage:
Wednesday
Sangeeta Mami called again. That's the third time this week.
When I got into the design course last year, she paid the whole fee. I cried, I touched her feet, I was so grateful. Now she wants me to live with her after the course "to help with the house" and she's started suggesting a boy from her friend's family.
When I hesitated today, she said, "Chandrika beti, I never asked for anything before."
I love her. I'm also starting to dread her calls.
I've decided: I'll thank her properly, from my heart, and tell her I'll visit every month and help with her shop's designs for free. But I'll live where my job is, and I'll choose who I marry. And I'll offer to repay the fee in instalments once I earn, so the gift stays a gift.
Tomorrow. In person. Not on the phone.

qa.q: What did Sangeeta Mami pay for?
qa.a: She paid the whole fee for Chandrika's design course.

qa.q: What mixed feelings does Chandrika have about Sangeeta Mami?
qa.a: Chandrika loves and feels grateful to her Mami, but also dreads her calls because the gift now comes with demands.

qa.q: What choice does Chandrika make to keep the relationship clean?
qa.a: She plans to thank Mami, offer help and visits by choice, keep her own decisions about home and marriage, and offer to repay the fee.

qa.q: How might Sangeeta Mami feel when Chandrika explains in person?
qa.a: Sangeeta Mami might feel hurt at first, but also respected because Chandrika thanks her warmly and comes in person.

grounding: A young adult whose relative paid her fees now faces demands for favours and control, and plans to accept kindly while keeping her freedom.

passage: When Sangeeta got the teaching job in Sangli, her Mama, Eshaan, arrived with a new scooter tied to a tempo. The whole lane came out to watch. "For our schoolteacher!" Sangeeta cried a little. Three months later the calls started. Could she drop his son at tuition every evening? Could she ask her principal to admit his friend's daughter? Last week: "After all I've done, you'll meet the boy I've chosen, no?" Sangeeta sat in the courtyard with the scooter key in her palm for a long time. Then she walked to his house. "Mama, I'm grateful. I'll still help with tuition drops when I can. But I can't pay for a gift with my choices. If it's that kind of gift, please take it back." He shouted. Her Mami quietly made tea. A week later he came to dinner and didn't mention the boy.

qa.q: Where did Sangeeta get the teaching job?
qa.a: She got the teaching job in Sangli.

qa.q: What was Sangeeta feeling as she sat in the courtyard with the key?
qa.a: Sangeeta felt torn and uneasy, grateful for the gift but trapped by what it was now being used to demand.

qa.q: What made Sangeeta's reply fair to both sides?
qa.a: She thanked Eshaan, offered the help she could really give, and calmly offered to return the scooter rather than trade her choices for it.

qa.q: How might Eshaan have seen his gift at first?
qa.a: Eshaan probably saw it as generous family love, and may have felt hurt and angry when Sangeeta refused to treat it as a debt, which is why he shouted.

grounding: It illustrates a young adult whose costly gift from a relative turns into a lever for control, and who keeps her freedom by thanking him and offering to give it back.
